statement: The user asked for a design of a field-service scheduling tool for Indian SMEs with 5-50 technicians coordinating over WhatsApp.
The product will hold customer names, phone numbers and addresses, which are personal data.

provenance.limitation: Follows from the stated use case, not from a data inventory.

statement: No brand, name screening or brandbook exists for this product; the design uses neutral tokens and a working title.
Owners or a dispatcher assign jobs over WhatsApp and phone calls.

provenance.limitation: From the brief wording; no interviews.

statement: Missed jobs, double bookings and missing job records are the costly failures of the current workaround.

provenance.limitation: Untested; the design's priorities depend on it.

statement: Technicians use low- to mid-range Android phones with intermittent connectivity in the field.

provenance.limitation: Plausible for the segment; not measured.

statement: Primary roles are dispatcher/owner and technician; the customer is off-platform and receives messages.
Current tools are WhatsApp groups, phone calls, paper diaries or spreadsheets.
Success means assigning a job in under 20 seconds on a phone and marking a job complete in under 10 seconds, with no job lost.

provenance.limitation: Targets invented to make the design testable; a PRD must confirm or replace them.

statement: English UI first with Hindi and one regional language planned; strings must tolerate longer translations.
Mobile web (Android browsers) first for technicians; desktop web for the dispatch board.
A single 'today' list per technician with one-tap status changes outperforms a calendar view for field use.

provenance.limitation: To be tested in usability sessions with real technicians.

statement: Dispatchers need a dense, scannable board (technician rows x time) on desktop and a list-first view on phone.
No PRD exists. Which jobs-to-be-done, roles and acceptance criteria are confirmed?
No brandbook or screened name exists. Which brand traits should the visual direction express?
No competitor pattern map exists. Differentiation cannot be assessed until one is produced by competitive-analysis.
Run the product-design workflow on hypothesis inputs to produce reviewable design artefacts; the design gate will record missing prerequisites as findings rather than pretend they exist.
Designing without customer research may optimise for the wrong task; every flow decision is traceable to an A- or H- entry so it can be revisited.

Rejected for v1: a drag-and-drop calendar as the technician's primary view. Reason: small screens, one-handed use and connectivity (A-003) favour a list; dragging also needs a single-pointer alternative (WCAG 2.5.7).
Rejected for v1: bulk actions on the dispatcher board; teams of 5-50 do not justify a selection model and its error states.
Rejected: a chat-style timeline mirroring WhatsApp as the primary model; it hides job status and ordering, which are the weaknesses the product exists to fix.

Of seven reachable competitor homepages captured on 2026-11-18, five use orange or saturated blue accents and five declare Inter-family geometric sans fonts; three lead with AI headlines (01-research/competitor-capture.json).

provenance.limitation: Marketing sites, not product UI; first linked stylesheets only.

statement: Anek is licensed under SIL OFL 1.1, is a variable font with weight and width axes, and covers Latin plus nine Indian scripts including Devanagari and Tamil.
Working title 'Kaamline' is unscreened in any trademark register and the 'Kaam' prefix is crowded in Indian field apps (KaamCam); it must not be published before counsel review.
Direction 1 'Whiteboard (ink + marker)' selected for development, pending brand gate and human approval; directions 2 and 3 rejected (X-004, X-005).
Does Anek support tabular figures (tnum) for time columns? Confirm before build.
Which OFL/MIT icon set will be used? Record in asset provenance before build.
